items.title: OpenAI gives eligible ChatGPT Pro and Business subscribers up to $500 a month in API credits
items.summary: Subscribers on eligible ChatGPT plans can now claim monthly API credits (up to $500, depending on plan) to build apps and agents, usable on the API's models such as GPT Live, Image 2.5 and the Decisions API. It ties the chat subscription to developer usage for the first time.

doubt.pushback: Replies say the amount varies by plan and the first grant is prorated to the billing cycle, so many see far less than $500 at first.

reception.summary: Welcomed as a way to turn a subscription into experiment budget; confusion over prorated first grants and per-plan amounts.

items.title: Claude Code CLI brings back 'ultrathink': one turn at xhigh effort, including subagents spawned in that turn
items.summary: Typing ultrathink in Claude Code raises reasoning effort to xhigh for a single turn, so you can keep Opus 5.5 on medium and spend extra thinking only where needed. Any subagents started during that turn also run at xhigh.

reception.summary: Users glad it is back; one asks whether it busts the prompt cache like other effort switches, another whether max effort actually helps.

items.title: Qwenputer: Qwen3.5-4B with a RISC-V CPU built into its weights runs C and MicroPython inside its forward pass
items.summary: The model uses its own Gated DeltaNet layers as RAM to emulate a CPU, so it executes code with no external runtime. On DeepMind math it reports 97.5-100% versus 55-90% for the base model and 95-100% with a Python tool. Witcheer reproduced it on one RTX 5090: asked for 2**200, the base model ran out of 4,096 tokens while Qwenputer printed all 61 digits.

items.title: Harbor v0.25.0 adds features to mitigate reward hacking in agent evals and RL environments
items.summary: The Harbor agent evaluation framework ships new safeguards against reward hacking, developed after outside researchers reported exploits in its tasks.

items.title: LiteLLM Autorouter SDK: pick a model per prompt in plain Python, no proxy needed
items.summary: Classify prompts with heuristics, an LLM or custom code, map tiers to any models, mix providers, pin sessions and escalate when a model stalls, all inside the LiteLLM Python SDK.

items.title: Sakana AI opens its API Platform to enterprise customers in early access
items.summary: Sakana's models are now available by API with organization management features; early access for enterprises starts today (announcement in Japanese).

items.title: AA-Robotics v0.1: Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra drive the same arm very differently (3,270 moves in 34 min vs 514 in 13 min)
items.summary: Artificial Analysis' new robotics eval shows frontier models controlling a real arm. Writing 'hello world', Claude dotted it out point by point while GPT-6 Astra drew continuous strokes, finishing in well under half the time.

items.title: fal Motion to Code: describe an animation or upload an image or video and get editable GSAP or GLSL code
items.summary: Outputs a GSAP web page or a looping GLSL shader instead of a video file: a few KB, sharp at any resolution and editable.

items.title: Vela 3.0 router (vela3-fast, 0.4B) ported to Core ML: about 10 ms per decision on an M5 Pro, matching the base model
items.summary: A community Core ML port with Swift code runs Vela 3.0's routing and PII span model on the Mac GPU. It matched the base on 1,200 of 1,200 decisions and caught 2,956 of 2,971 planted personal details in a 20,000-word file, fully on device. Follows the Vela 3.0 release kept this morning.

items.title: FACT: a fast 'cerebellum' robot policy trained on 2,000 hours of human video with tactile forces
items.summary: A slow planner predicts video and actions while a fast force-action refiner uses touch feedback. Pretrained on the new EgoForce dataset (40,000 episodes, 1,000 tasks) and fine-tuned on 10 robot plus 90 human demos per task, it beats pi0.5 and T-Rex on 10 real tasks; force labels lift test-tube cap opening from 0% to 80%.

items.title: EmbeddingGemma 2 tech report published
items.summary: Google's technical report for EmbeddingGemma 2 is now on arXiv, covering how the embedding model was built and evaluated.

items.title: DeepSeek Harness (DSH) 0.2.2-alpha.2 can dispatch Codex and Claude Code as subagents
items.summary: A new subagent_oar tool merges the separate Codex and Claude Code plugins, so a DeepSeek model can plan and hand tasks to either agent; the release also adds worktree-isolated sessions and per-step context and cache stats. CLI only for now; setup needs two packages and a config edit, and Codex gets full file access by default.

items.title: Decagon runs an AutoResearch loop on SGLang: agents diagnose inference bottlenecks and test fixes on replayed production traffic
items.summary: Decagon describes agents that find serving bottlenecks, try changes against replays of real traffic and keep only verified gains, built on its SGLang stack.
